{
"title": "Tumor PD-L1 selectively suppresses type I interferon in myeloid cells to suppress CTL recruitment to promote lung metastasis",
"authors": "John D Klement; Priscilla S Redd; Chunwan Lu; Alyssa D Merting; Dakota B Poschel; Dafeng Yang; Gang Zhou; David H Munn; Kebin Liu",
"field_subfield": "Cancer immunology / tumor immunology",
"type_of_paper": "Primary research (experimental study)",
"executive_summary": "This study re-examines the long-held view that tumor PD-L1 (tPD-L1) suppresses cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) directly through PD-1 engagement. The authors demonstrate that tPD-L1 has no direct effect on CTL activation or lytic function when only tumor cells and tumor-specific CTLs are present. Instead, tPD-L1 acts indirectly by engaging PD-1 on myeloid cells (mPD-1), which suppresses type I interferon (IFN-I) and STAT1 signaling, represses the chemokines Cxcl9 and Cxcl10, and thereby impairs CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Critically, knocking out PD-L1 in tumor cells does not affect primary tumor growth but significantly decreases lung metastasis in a CTL-dependent manner. Using murine triple-negative breast cancer (4T1) and colorectal cancer (CT26) cell lines, the researchers showed that loss of PD-L1 increased CD3+ T cell infiltration at metastatic sites without altering initial disseminated tumor cell colonization. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that tPD-L1 loss drives transcriptional changes in myeloid cells rather than CTLs, enhancing antigen presentation and PD-L2 expression. Depletion of myeloid cells with clodronate liposomes diminished tPD-L1's promotion of lung metastasis, confirming that myeloid cells bridge tPD-L1 to CTL suppression. The work also extends to human patients with metastatic basal cell carcinoma, showing that response to PD-1 blockade correlates with IFN-I response in myeloid cells. The authors propose that the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis controls CTL tumor infiltration in lung metastasis, which underlies the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in the neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings. This reframes tPD-L1 as a driver of metastatic immune evasion rather than a direct shield against CTL-mediated tumor cell lysis, with implications for understanding why some tumors respond to PD-1 blockade and for optimizing combination therapies involving type I interferon agonists. The study highlights the importance of the metastatic niche and myeloid cell populations in mediating tPD-L1's effects, offering new insights into the mechanisms of immune evasion and potential therapeutic targets for improving cancer immunotherapy outcomes.",
"research_context": [
  { "PD-L1 and PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade immunotherapy is believed to function by blocking the engagement of PD-L1 to co-inhibitory receptor PD-1 expressed by activated and exhausted cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs).": "co-inhibitory receptor PD-1 expressed by activated and exhausted cytotoxic T lymphocytes" },
  { "PD-1 engagement on CTLs has been shown to result in decreased activation and effector functions due to SHP-2 mediated dephosphorylation of the T cell receptor and CD28 signaling cascades, driving CTLs toward an exhausted fate.": "SHP-2 mediated dephosphorylation of the T cell receptor" },
  { "Particular attention has been paid to the role of tumor-expressed PD-L1 (tPD-L1), which has been hypothesized to serve as a direct molecular shield against CTL lysis of tumor cells.": "direct molecular shield against CTL lysis of tumor cells" },
  { "Emerging experimental data has started to reveal alternative pathways to this paradigm, and suggest that response of CTLs to PD-1/L1 blockade may depend on tumor anatomic sites and occur principally in other sites, rather than the primary tumor site.": "response of CTLs to PD-1/L1 blockade may depend on tumor anatomic sites" },
  { "As the dominant cause of mortality is metastatic growth, the durable survival benefit conferred by PD-1/L1 blockade thus arises from coordinated suppression of metastases.": "the dominant cause of mortality is metastatic growth" },
  { "Robust tumor expression of PD-L1 has been shown to promote both micro-and macro-metastatic tumor growth, with enhancement at metastatic tumor sites as compared to primary tumor sites.": "enhancement at metastatic tumor sites as compared to primary tumor sites" },
  { "However, how tPD-L1 might differentially drive metastasis from primary tumor is unknown.": "how tPD-L1 might differentially drive metastasis from primary tumor is unknown" },
  { "Emerging experimental data over the past decade has highlighted the importance of PD-1 expression in other cell populations, including myeloid, dendritic, and tumor cells, in tumor immune evasion.": "importance of PD-1 expression in other cell populations" },
  { "However, how non-T cell-expressed PD-1 connects tPD-L1 to CTL suppression is incompletely understood.": "how non-T cell-expressed PD-1 connects tPD-L1 to CTL suppression is incompletely understood" }
],

  { "The authors hypothesized that tPD-L1 exhibits no direct effect on CTL activity when only tumor cells and tumor-specific CTLs are present.": "tPD-L1 exhibits no direct effect on CTL activity when only tumor cells and tumor-specific CTLs are present" },

  { "The authors hypothesized that this attenuation of type I interferon signaling was mediated by tPD-L1 engagement with PD-1 found on lung-resident myeloid cells.": "tPD-L1 engagement with PD-1 found on lung-resident myeloid cells" },

{
"title": "Tumor PD-L1 selectively suppresses type I interferon in myeloid cells to suppress CTL recruitment to promote lung metastasis",
"authors": "John D Klement; Priscilla S Redd; Chunwan Lu; Alyssa D Merting; Dakota B Poschel; Dafeng Yang; Gang Zhou; David H Munn; Kebin Liu",
"field_subfield": "Cancer immunology / tumor immunology (metastasis & immune checkpoint blockade)",
"type_of_paper": "Primary research article (experimental study with in vitro, in vivo, and human patient data)",
"executive_summary": "This study re-examines the canonical view that tumor-expressed PD-L1 (tPD-L1) suppresses cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) directly through CTL PD-1. The authors demonstrate that tPD-L1 has no direct effect on CTL activation or lytic function when only tumor cells and CTLs are present. Instead, tPD-L1 acts indirectly by engaging PD-1 on myeloid cells (mPD-1), which suppresses type I interferon (IFN-I) and STAT1 signaling, repressing the chemokines Cxcl9 and Cxcl10, and thereby impairing CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Critically, knocking out PD-L1 in tumor cells does not affect primary tumor growth but significantly decreases lung metastasis in a CTL-dependent manner. Depletion of myeloid cells using clodronate liposomes impaired tPD-L1 promotion of lung metastasis, confirming the myeloid intermediary role. summary.title: Tumor PD-L1 selectively suppresses type I interferon in myeloid cells to suppress CTL recruitment to promote lung metastasis
summary.authors: John D Klement; Priscilla S Redd; Chunwan Lu; Alyssa D Merting; Dakota B Poschel; Dafeng Yang; Gang Zhou; David H Munn; Kebin Liu
summary.field_subfield: Cancer immunology / tumor immunology (metastasis & immune checkpoint blockade)
summary.type_of_paper: Primary research article (experimental study with in vitro, in vivo, and human patient data)
summary.executive_summary: This study re-examines the canonical view that tumor-expressed PD-L1 (tPD-L1) suppresses cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) directly through CTL PD-1. The authors demonstrate that tPD-L1 has no direct effect on CTL activation or lytic function when only tumor cells and CTLs are present. Instead, tPD-L1 acts indirectly by engaging PD-1 on myeloid cells (mPD-1), which suppresses type I interferon (IFN-I) and STAT1 signaling, repressing the chemokines Cxcl9 and Cxcl10, and thereby impairing CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Critically, knocking out PD-L1 in tumor cells does not affect primary tumor growth but significantly decreases lung metastasis in a CTL-dependent manner. Depletion of myeloid cells using clodronate liposomes impaired tPD-L1 promotion of lung metastasis, confirming the myeloid intermediary role. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that tPD-L1 engages myeloid PD-1 to antagonize IFN-I and STAT1 signaling to repress Cxcl9 and Cxcl10 expression to impair CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Human patient response to PD-1 blockade immunotherapy correlates with IFN-I response in myeloid cells. The data establish that the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis controls CTL tumor infiltration in lung metastasis. The work uses murine triple negative breast cancer (4T1) and colorectal cancer (CT26) cell lines, an in vitro CTL-tumor interaction system with the 2/20 CTL line, orthotopic and experimental metastasis models, RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and a human patient cohort with metastatic basal cell carcinoma. The findings suggest that tPD-L1 may control CTL recruitment versus functionality, and that low response rates in interferon alpha therapies may be due to compensatory PD-1/L1 upregulation. The study has limitations, including exclusive analysis of lung metastases, which may have a uniquely inflamed microenvironment. The paper does not report data/code availability, ethical considerations, or key figures/tables in the provided text, and the bibliography is omitted, so top_influential_citations is empty.

claims.description: tPD-L1 suppresses CTL recruitment to lung metastases via the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis, independent of primary tumor growth.
The PD-1/L1 axis functions as a negative feedback circuit for type I interferon signaling.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study re-examines the canonical view that tumor-expressed PD-L1 (tPD-L1) suppresses cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) directly through CTL PD-1. The authors demonstrate that tPD-L1 has no direct effect on CTL activation or lytic function when only tumor cells and CTLs are present. Instead, tPD-L1 acts indirectly by engaging PD-1 on myeloid cells (mPD-1), which suppresses type I interferon (IFN-I) and STAT1 signaling, repressing the chemokines Cxcl9 and Cxcl10, and thereby impairing CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Critically, knocking out PD-L1 in tumor cells does not affect primary tumor growth but significantly decreases lung metastasis in a CTL-dependent manner. Depletion of myeloid cells using clodronate liposomes impaired tPD-L1 promotion of lung metastasis, confirming the myeloid intermediary role. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that tPD-L1 engages myeloid PD-1 to antagonize IFN-I and STAT1 signaling to repress Cxcl9 and Cxcl10 expression to impair CTL recruitment to lung metastases. Human patient response to PD-1 blockade immunotherapy correlates with IFN-I response in myeloid cells. The data establish that the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis controls CTL tumor infiltration in lung metastasis. The work uses murine triple negative breast cancer (4T1) and colorectal cancer (CT26) cell lines, an in vitro CTL-tumor interaction system with the 2/20 CTL line, orthotopic and experimental metastasis models, RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and a human patient cohort with metastatic basal cell carcinoma. The findings suggest that tPD-L1 may control CTL recruitment versus functionality, and that low response rates in interferon alpha therapies may be due to compensatory PD-1/L1 upregulation. The study has limitations, including exclusive analysis of lung metastases, which may have a uniquely inflamed microenvironment. The paper does not report data/code availability, ethical considerations, or key figures/tables in the provided text, and the bibliography is omitted, so top_influential_citations is empty.

Research Context
The mechanism of PD-L1/PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade is well-established for CTLs. PD-1 engagement on CTLs decreases activation and effector functions. The role of tumor-expressed PD-L1 as a direct molecular shield is hypothesized. PD-1 expression in non-T cell populations is increasingly recognized. How non-T cell-expressed PD-1 connects tPD-L1 to CTL suppression is unclear. The differential role of tPD-L1 in driving metastasis versus primary tumor is unknown.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether tPD-L1 directly suppresses CTLs or acts through an intermediate cell. The hypothesis is that tPD-L1 targets myeloid cell PD-1 to suppress type I interferon. The predicted outcome is that this represses Cxcl9 and Cxcl10 to impair CTL recruitment. The authors predict tPD-L1 promotes lung metastasis independent of primary tumor growth. The authors predict myeloid cells bridge tPD-L1 to CTL suppression. The authors predict human response to PD-1 blockade correlates with myeloid IFN-I response.

Methodological Details
The study used murine triple negative breast cancer 4T1 and colorectal cancer CT26 cell lines. PD-L1 was deleted by knocking out Cd274 in both cell lines. The in vitro CTL-tumor interaction system used the 2/20 tumor-specific CTL line. The 2/20 CTL line recognizes the H2-Ld-restricted AH1 epitope of gp70. PD-L1 KO cells showed no PD-L2 expression, the only alternative PD-1 ligand. Primary tumor growth was assessed via orthotopic injection into syngeneic mice. No difference was observed in primary tumor growth between WT and PD-L1 KO. Lung metastasis was assessed via tail vein injection and lung quantification. Lungs were harvested, inflated with India ink, and quantified. Myeloid cells were depleted using clodronate liposomes in tumor-bearing mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on CD45+ leukocytes from colonized lungs. Approximately 7500 cells were analyzed by UMAP clustering. Cell populations were annotated by comparison to publicly available datasets. Flow cytometry confirmed transcript-level observations in lung myeloid cells. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed after seven days of tumor colonization. Single-cell libraries were generated using the Chromium Single Cell 3' Reagent Kit v3. High quality cells were defined by feature count and mitochondrial read thresholds. Cells were clustered using the first fifty principal components. The human cohort included patients with metastatic basal cell carcinoma. Single-cell sequencing was performed before and after PD-1 blockade. Statistical analysis used Prism8 and two-tailed Student's t-test. Survival analysis used two-sided log-rank test in the Survival package. Cell lines were obtained from ATCC and tested bi-monthly for mycoplasma. RAW264.7 macrophages were used for in vitro co-culture experiments. Random seed, train/test split, and patient demographics are not reported.

Procedures And Architectures
CRISPR lentivirus was produced by co-transfecting HEK293FT cells. Tumor cells were transduced with lentivirus and selected with puromycin. Bulk cells were sorted for marker-negative cells using BD FACSARIA. 4T1 orthotopic tumors were established at the right second mammary gland. CT26 subcutaneous tumors were established at the right flank. Neutralization experiments used anti-CD8α or isotype control antibodies. Flow cytometry samples were blocked in FACS Buffer with mouse FcBlock. Flow cytometry data was analyzed with FlowJo v10.6.0. RNA was extracted using Direct-zol RNA microprep kit. RNA was sequenced by Novogene. Reads were aligned to the reference genome using STARv2.5. Reads were quantified using HTSeqv0.6.1. GSEA was performed using GSEA4.0 with gene-set permutation. GO pathway enrichment was performed with clusterprofiler. Leukocytes were positively selected using CD45 magnetic nanobeads. Cell viability was assessed using trypan blue with ≥ 80% viable cells. Cells were loaded to capture approximately 2-3 x 10^3 targeted cells. Sequencing was performed on Illumina NextSeq 500 platform. Alignment generated 30-39K reads/cell with 75-102 million reads per sample. Approximately 1600 median genes per cell were obtained. Doublet removal was performed by DoubletFinder. Cells were annotated by comparison to pre-existing datasets using SingleR. The tPD-L1 loss gene signature required at least two-fold increase with padj < 0.05. The SHP-2 activation signature used SHP099 treatment with two-fold increase. Macrophage PHATE clusters were transferred to human lung macrophage dataset. Cluster-identifying signatures were calculated by Seurat FindAllMarkers. Batch effects were corrected by Harmony in patient dataset analysis. The tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis was determined to control CTL infiltration. The negative feedback circuit links PD-1/L1 axis to type I interferon signaling.

Key Results
tPD-L1 confers no survival advantage when CTL encounters a tumor cell. No difference was observed in primary tumor growth between WT and PD-L1 KO. No differences in tumor growth were observed in WT and PD-L1 KO CT26. Increased infiltration of CD3+ cells was observed in lung after loss of tPD-L1. No difference in initial tumor cell colonization was seen one day after injection. PD-L1-deficient and competent 4T1 metastasized equally in RAGII-KO mice. Genetic ablation of MHC class I and CD8+ depletion revealed CTL suppression. Myeloid cell surface PD-1 expression was enhanced following tPD-L1 loss. RAW surface PD-1 was upregulated in a cell-contact and IFNAR-dependent manner. Engagement with tPD-L1 enhanced SHP-2 activation and decreased pSTAT1. Diminished MHC class II expression was observed on both 4T1 and RAW cells. RAW PD-1 loss led to increased sensitivity to poly(I:C) stimulation. Disruption of PD-1 enhanced IFNβ production. Differential expression of PD-L2 was observed as early as one day after injection. This increase occurred before robust infiltration and activation of CTLs. Depletion of myeloid cells diminished tPD-L1 function in promoting tumor growth. Myeloid cell PHATE analysis revealed differentiation restriction released following PD-1 blockade. Release led to enhanced interferon signaling, antigen presentation, and chemokine expression. Mouse myeloid cluster identities were transferred to human lung myeloid dataset. The tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis controls CTL tumor infiltration.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
tPD-L1 uncouples its role at the metastatic site from primary tumor. tPD-L1 binds mPD-1 to enforce an immunologically cold microenvironment. tPD-L1 may control CTL recruitment versus functionality. The PD-1/L1 axis functions as a negative feedback circuit for IFN-I. Low response rates in interferon alpha therapies may be due to compensatory PD-1/L1. Suppression of interferon signaling is a primary mechanism of immune evasion. Type I interferon signaling is essential for myeloid cell function in CTL recruitment. The axis underlies the efficacy of ICB in neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study exclusively analyzed lung metastases, which may have a uniquely inflamed microenvironment. Conflicting findings exist for the role of tPD-L1 in PD-1 blockade efficacy. tPD-L1 may be sufficient but not necessary for response in primary tumors. The effect of PD-1 blockade on CTLs may occur in secondary lymphoid structures. The study focuses on CTL recruitment, not CTL functionality, in metastasis. The negative feedback circuit hypothesis requires further validation. The human cohort is limited to metastatic basal cell carcinoma.

Claims
tPD-L1 suppresses CTL recruitment to lung metastases via the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis, independent of primary tumor growth. tPD-L1 confers no survival advantage when CTL encounters a tumor cell. No difference was observed in primary tumor growth between WT and PD-L1 KO. tPD-L1 targets myeloid cell-expressed PD-1 to suppress type I IFN. tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis controls CTL tumor infiltration. Depletion of myeloid cells diminished tPD-L1 function in promoting tumor growth. tPD-L1 may be sufficient but not necessary for response in primary tumors. Conflicting findings exist for the role of tPD-L1 in PD-1 blockade efficacy. The study exclusively analyzed lung metastases, which may have a uniquely inflamed microenvironment. The axis underlies the efficacy of ICB in neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings. Low response rates in interferon alpha therapies may be due to compensatory PD-1/L1. Suppression of interferon signaling is a primary mechanism of immune evasion. Human response to PD-1 blockade correlates with myeloid IFN-I response.
The PD-1/L1 axis functions as a negative feedback circuit for type I interferon signaling. The PD-1/L1 axis is induced by and then attenuates type I interferon signaling. Disruption of PD-1 enhanced IFNβ production. Type I interferon induces both PD-L1 and PD-1 in myeloid cells. PD-L1 expression is upregulated more rapidly than PD-1. The study exclusively analyzed lung metastases, which may have a uniquely inflamed microenvironment. Early success for interferon or TLR/STING agonists combined with anti-PD-1/L1. Mutations in interferon pathway are associated with adaptive resistance to immunotherapy. Forced overexpression of Irf7 abrogated triple negative breast cancer bone metastasis.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Depletion of myeloid cells diminished tPD-L1 function in promoting tumor growth. Genetic ablation of MHC class I and CD8+ depletion revealed CTL suppression. RAW PD-1 loss led to increased sensitivity to poly(I:C) stimulation. Disruption of PD-1 enhanced IFNβ production. PD-L1 KO cells showed no PD-L2 expression, the only alternative PD-1 ligand.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the tPD-L1/mPD-1/IFN-I/STAT1/Cxcl9/10 axis controlling CTL infiltration. 2. The strongest evidence is the myeloid depletion and single-cell RNA sequencing findings. 3. The future path is extending beyond lung metastases and validating the negative feedback circuit.
